painting.title: God Creating the World
painting.institution: The Morgan Library & Museum, Morgan Family Collection

records.subject: Exact Genesis creation subject; represents the opening of Genesis, not all four Easter Vigil prophecies.
records.identity: Official indexed Morgan record verifies the physical watercolor. Its title/artist match the approved Holy Saturday label; selected-file visual match remains pending.

image.access: Object page returns 403 to direct research-browser access; indexed institutional metadata exposes a Download label. No bytes acquired.

rights.photo: Morgan website downloads are restricted to personal, educational or noncommercial use and must remain unaltered. High-resolution publication uses require the institution's paid process. Not suitable for unrestricted app reuse under this route.
rights.alternative: Seek an independently digitized historical edition that can be matched to this composition; no qualifying alternate located. Do not substitute a scan of another Tissot Genesis scene.

records.mobile: Portrait; full image only pending visual QA.

records.identity: Physical Getty work verified. The date-selection overlay names title and artist without a specific image; match to the approved reproduction remains pending. Do not confuse this finished watercolor with Martin's separate mezzotint.

image.dimensionEvidence: Commons original-file listing, not local byte verification
image.provenance: Commons cites Getty object 103QTX, labels the reproduction CC0, and embeds Getty accession 2018.45 in image metadata.

rights.photo: CC0 explicitly recorded for this Getty-derived file. Getty's current policy confirms CC0 for its Open Content reproductions, including commercial reuse.
rights.credit: The J. Paul Getty Museum, Los Angeles, 2018.45
rights.limitation: The current Getty object page needs JavaScript; file-to-object crosswalk uses institutional exhibition caption plus source metadata.

records.identity: Current institutional record transcribes John Bridges / Roma 1833. Commons says 1839; prefer 1833 in this research supplement and retain the discrepancy for file/inscription comparison. The active dates 1818–1854 should not be asserted as birth/death years.
